review_candidates.title: Infrastructure operations Engineer
review_candidates.description: Infrastructure Operations Engineer (Linux) — 24x7 GPU Data Centre Remote-first (with 2 days per week down the line once they open their Aztec West office) · £50,000–£65,000 depending on level (L2/L3) · 4-on-4-off shift · Permanent I'm working with an AI infrastructure company that builds and operates GPU data centres across the UK, converting legacy industrial and energy sites into modern, renewable-powered compute. They're about a year in, backed by around half a billion in investment, running modular data centres packed with Nvidia GPUs, and currently building out their second and third sites. Their compute powers a single, highly technical customer running large-scale AI workloads. This is genuinely new national infrastructure, and they're standing up the operations function that keeps it running. I'm looking for someone who joins early enough to shape how it works. What I'm looking for This isn't a first-line "watch the dashboard and escalate" seat. I need an engineer who owns and resolves. You'd be the technical owner of live GPU infrastructure performance, reliability and security. When something breaks, you diagnose it, root-cause it and fix it, rather than passing it up the chain. You'd handle genuinely technical incidents and tickets from a technical customer (no end users), coordinate maintenance and change, work closely with the build and site partners, and help design the runbooks, tooling and monitoring that a young operation is still building from scratch. Because it's early-stage, there's real autonomy, real visibility with leadership, and a direct hand in how they operate at scale as they grow. What you'd actually do Own and resolve complex incidents across GPU compute, storage, networking and the wider platform, working at the Linux command line rather than escalating first. Root-cause analysis and permanent fixes, not just symptom clearing. Build and improve monitoring, alerting and automation so the platform runs cleaner over time. Coordinate maintenance windows, changes and site work with engineering, field and Smart Hands partners. Own technical tickets end to end, keep documentation and knowledge current, and run clean shift handovers. Help set the operational standards for a function that's still being built. What you'll need Professional Linux experience. You're comfortable administering and troubleshooting Linux (RHEL or similar) at the command line in a production environment. This is a hard requirement, not a nice-to-have. An infrastructure background (servers, compute, storage, virtualisation), rather than a purely network one. Automation and scripting (Ansible, Python, Bash or similar) and the instinct to build rather than just operate off-the-shelf tools. Real incident-resolution experience at 2nd or 3rd line, owning problems through to resolution under SLA. You're comfortable working a 24x7, 4-on-4-off shift pattern (12-hour days and nights). Eligible for UK Security Clearance (SC), which will be needed within the first year, and a full UK driving licence . Located within reach of Bristol for the occasional office day. Nice to have GPU, HPC or AI infrastructure exposure; monitoring stacks (Grafana, Prometheus, Zabbix, Nagios, SolarWinds); Kubernetes, Terraform or IaC; ITIL awareness; cloud, hosting, data centre or MSP operations. The shift pattern, honestly It's a genuine 24x7 shift role including nights, but the 4-on-4-off pattern is predictable and gives you large blocks of time off, effectively around half the month. You'll know your schedule well in advance rather than being permanently on call. Why I think it's worth a look Cutting-edge Nvidia GPU infrastructure at real scale, a well-funded company building critical national infrastructure, genuine autonomy to shape how operations run, and the chance to grow with a business that's scaling fast. If you want to own and build rather than just monitor, this is the one. If that sounds like you, get in touch and I'll tell you more.

review_candidates.description: Job Title Description The Space Telescope Science Institute (STScI), operated by the Association of Universities for Research in Astronomy (AURA), is NASA's science operations center for missions including the Hubble and James Webb Space Telescopes. STScI leads observation planning, data analysis, public engagement, and data archiving for flagship missions. Our staff include experts in astronomy, engineering, education, information technology, communications, and administration who work together to advance and share discoveries from space. STScI is seeking an Enterprise Technology Lead to set the direction for enterprise information technology across the institute, drive modernization, and serve as the institute’s senior IT advisor across mission, engineering, and business functions. This position supports hybrid or fully remote work arrangements. Candidates must reside in MD, DE, VA, PA, DC, or WV. Hybrid staff are expected on-site a minimum of three days per week. U.S. Citizenship or Permanent Residency required; ITAR clearance required. Enterprise Technology Lead Role And Responsibilities This role is ideal for a senior information technology leader who operates at enterprise altitude while remaining willing and able to engage substantively with technical work when the situation demands it. The Enterprise Technology Lead reports to the Head of IT and co-chairs the enterprise technology governance body. The position emphasizes strategic technology direction, modernization leadership, portfolio and financial discipline, and trusted advisory engagement across the institute. This is a hands-on leadership role that blends strategy with execution, working closely with Chief Engineers, mission leadership, IT operations, and division stakeholders to ensure technology decisions are coherent, sustainable, and aligned with the institute’s long-term direction. Key Responsibilities: Enterprise Technology Strategy & Governance Co-chair the enterprise technology governance body and drive cross-functional decision-making across mission and business functions. Assist in the development and execution of a multi-year enterprise technology roadmap aligned with mission, engineering, and institutional business objectives. Own enterprise information technology architecture and integration strategy across mission systems, enterprise platforms, and shared services. Serve as trusted technology advisor to senior leaders, managers and institute staff on how technology can improve efficiency, delivery, and decision-making. Lead IT product roadmap validation, technology lifecycle governance, and technical due diligence. Cloud-First & Run-Anywhere Strategy Help set enterprise direction for a cloud-first posture spanning public cloud, private cloud, and SaaS. Lead modernization of the on-premises data center to operate as a private cloud with workload portability across environments. Govern SaaS migration strategy, infrastructure as code, cloud integration patterns, and workload placement principles. Support the Cloud Center of Excellence to balance performance, cost, and operational fit across environments. Technology Portfolio & Financial Governance Drive continuous rationalization of the enterprise technology portfolio and active decommissioning of redundant tools and systems. Establish and govern a consistent framework for evaluating technology investments, renewals, and consolidation opportunities. Build enterprise-wide financial visibility across the technology portfolio and lead TCO modeling for current and future-state environments. Partner with finance and operational stakeholders to communicate investment rationale and reduce the cost of running enterprise IT. Identity, Security & AI Governance Govern enterprise identity and access management strategy and Zero Trust posture. Align security posture to certification and regulatory standards including ITAR. Monitor and enforce enterprise AI governance policy consistent with NASA policy requirements and responsible use standards. Lead enterprise AI enablement to amplify workforce effectiveness while maintaining clear guardrails. Institutional Leadership & Advisory Serve as trusted technology advisor to institutional leadership across science, engineering, and business functions. Represent the IT division in committees, working groups, and cross-divisional forums. Lead enterprise communications for technology change management. Coordinate cross-mission systems integration across NASA and AURA centers. Drive process improvement and modernization initiatives. Your Experience, Skills & Qualifications: 7+ years in a senior technology leadership capacity at enterprise scale. Demonstrated technical depth across cloud environments, enterprise data centers, private cloud, containerization, virtualization, storage, and infrastructure as code. 5+ years leading on premises to SaaS migration programs at enterprise scale. 2+ years defining and governing enterprise IAM strategy, with demonstrated experience integrating modern identity providers alongside Active Directory. Demonstrated experience governing enterprise application portfolios. Demonstrated AI policy development and enterprise AI service introduction. Track record leading enterprise technology modernization, portfolio rationalization, or major platform transitions. Direct accountability for aligning architecture with regulatory and compliance requirements (ITAR, federal standards). Experience developing and executing multi-year enterprise technology roadmaps. Familiarity with NIST 800-53 and NIST 800-171 security control frameworks preferred. Hands-on Kubernetes experience across on-premises and cloud environments preferred. Observability and SIEM platform experience (Datadog, Splunk, or CrowdStrike) preferred. Experience operating in federal, research, or mission-driven technology environments preferred. Relevant certifications in cloud, cybersecurity, or enterprise architecture (AWS, Azure, CISSP, TOGAF, or similar) preferred. The substitution of additional relevant education and/or experience for stated qualifications may be considered. Salary range is $180,000 to $195,000. Final compensation is based on experience, skills, internal equity, and market conditions. The posted salary range represents a general guideline. STScI considers several factors when determining salary offers, including internal equity, position scope and responsibilities, candidate qualifications, experience, education, skills, and current market conditions.
